title: Certified Phenom Instructor exam
rulesHtml:
Certified Phenom Instructor exam

Forty questions in three parts. Sixty minutes. Pass with 32 of 40 and no part below its floor.

Before you start

  • When to take it. On demand, after Lesson 20, when the drills in Lessons 9, 15 and 16 feel calm.
  • Time. 60 minutes for all three parts. Work in any order.
  • What you may use. Your soroban for Parts A and B. A pencil and this paper. Nothing else.
  • What you may not use. A calculator, the trainer, the course notes, or another person. Question 24 is mental: no soroban and no paper for that one.
  • How to answer. Part A: name the move and write its spoken line. Part B: write the answer (and, for 25 and 26, every rod move in order). Part C: circle one letter.

How it is marked

PartWhat it testsQuestionsFloor
ABead-move classification1–129 of 12
BWorked problems13–2610 of 14
CTeaching scenarios27–4010 of 14
AllPass mark4032 of 40 (80%)

One point per question. No half points. You pass when your total is 32 or more and every part meets its floor. If you miss, you get your score for each part and can retake whenever you are ready, on a fresh form. After a second miss, the Pass Promise starts: one-on-one coaching until you pass.

parts.title: Bead moves
parts.introHtml: The ones rod shows the first number. The tens rod has room to carry and beads to lend. For each one, name the move (free beads, small friend, big friend, or both friends at once), write it as a formula, and write the line a child says.

parts.title: Worked problems
parts.introHtml: Work each problem left to right. Write only the answer, except 25 and 26.

questions.text: A parent at pickup asks, "Will this help my son's ADHD?" What do you say?

options.label: "Yes. Hunter had ADHD, and look what happened to him."
"Studies show it improves focus and attention."
"I can't promise anything about ADHD, and the beads aren't a treatment. What the method builds is arithmetic speed and accuracy, fifteen minutes a day."
"It works for every child, so it will work for him."

questions.text: A Stage 2 child's rod shows 4. The next line is +1. She freezes for ten seconds. What do you do?

options.label: Ask "Free beads, or friend?" and wait.
Say "Bring the five down and take away four."
Move the beads slowly so she can watch.
Skip the problem so she doesn't get upset.

questions.text: A child gets 7 of 10 on the speed round, fast. What do you do?

options.label: Push for 10 of 10 at the same speed tomorrow.
Say "slow is fine," time nothing for a week, and bring the clock back when accuracy is 9 of 10.
Move on to the next lesson, since 7 is close.
Add more problems to the drill so the child gets more practice.

questions.text: A child takes the Explorer boss. Parts one and three pass. Part two (2-digit, four lines) scores 4 of 6. What next?

options.label: Restart Stage 2 from the first lesson.
Retry the boss right away while the moves are fresh.
Open Stage 3, since two of three parts passed.
Spend three days on the 2-digit small-friend lessons, then retry the boss.

questions.text: A child clears rung 11 of the Bead Score. Her father asks, "So she's 7th kyu now?" What do you say?

options.label: "Yes, she's officially 7th kyu."
"She cleared rung 11. That's about 7th kyu on the Japanese flash ladder. We're set against those grades, but we don't award them."
"Kyu grades don't mean anything."
"She'll be 1st kyu by the end of the year."

questions.text: A parent asks whether she could teach this too, and how much instructors make. What may you say?

options.label: "Most instructors land between $20 and $40 a session. Your rates are yours to set."
"You can easily make $2,000 a month."
"Enough to pay for your child's lessons, guaranteed."
"Most instructors replace their full-time income in a year."

questions.text: In a flash round, a child loses track at the fourth number. What do you say?

options.label: "Try to remember the numbers I said."
"Let's do that one again, slower."
"Let it go. Next one."
"You need to concentrate harder."

questions.text: Halfway through a mental sum, a child says, "I lost it." What is the fix?

options.label: Give the answer so the child can move on.
Tell the child to say the running total out loud.
Make the next round shorter.
Do the same sum once on the real soroban, close eyes, replay it, then the next one in the head.

questions.text: When do you speed up the flash tempo for a child?

options.label: When the child is right nine times out of ten at the current tempo.
Every week, on a fixed schedule.
When the child asks to go faster.
When the child is right half the time.

questions.text: A Stage 1 child takes six seconds to read 47 and her lips move as she looks at the beads. What do you do?

options.label: Read the number for her, then have her repeat it.
Use the peek: show the number for about two seconds, then cover it.
Let her count, since speed comes later.
Move her on to adding.

questions.text: Your class has three kids at Stage 2 and three at Stage 3. How do you run it?

options.label: Teach the Stage 3 lesson to everyone, since it's harder.
Teach the Stage 2 lesson to everyone, since it's easier.
Split the room: each group gets its own demo while the other does its written drill, then swap.
Send the Stage 2 kids home with worksheets.

questions.text: A child still forgets the small-friend take-aways after nine days. What do you do?

options.label: Keep drilling the take-aways until they stick.
Move on, since they'll pick it up in Stage 3.
Give a written list of the formulas to memorize.
Go back to the small-friend adds, repeat that drill until it passes three days running, then come forward.

questions.text: A parent of an online student asks if she can leave the room during the video lesson. What do you say?

options.label: "Sure, I'll keep an eye on him."
"Please stay in the room with the camera on for the whole lesson."
"Yes, as long as he has his soroban."
"Yes, but check in halfway through."

questions.text: Which of these may you promise the parent of a child starting Stage 1?

options.label: "By the end of the first stage, your child will read any number off the beads in a glance, and add and take away when the beads are free."
"Her school grades will go up within two weeks."
"His IQ will rise by the end of the year."
"This will improve her memory and attention."
